message: Writing the guide from what the agent found
Re-checking 8 key claims against their sources

text: I'll fetch all these URLs together in a single batch of calls.

Checking c19 against the policy: it requires review and approval for substantive modifications before reusing X Content for new purposes, and usage beyond the allowed scope requires an Enterprise plan — this matches the policy language directly.

For c2, the Composio KB confirms managed credentials were removed in Feb 2026 and now a custom X developer app plus custom auth config is required — supported.

c6 matches the developer-account page flow: login, email verification, possibly phone, entering name/location/use case, accepting the agreement, and confirming via email — supported.

c1 doesn't hold up since the managed-auth page loads its toolkit list dynamically and doesn't explicitly state Twitter isn't managed, so I'm marking it as not_found.

For c4, the bearer token details and endpoint list (search, post lookup, usage, compliance, label-stream) line up with the KB, and I'm checking the explanation for 401 errors around mismatched bearer tokens.

c5 checks out — the page's guidance on fixing EXPIRED connections and typical causes of errors matches the claim closely enough.

c26 is only partially supported since the policy page covers suspension for violations and use-case deviations but doesn't actually enumerate "official rejection reasons."

c7 matches the composio.dev walkthrough for creating an X app via console.x.com — navigating to Apps, creating the app, configuring OAuth 2.0 user authentication, selecting app type, adding a callback, and saving the client ID/secret — fully supported.

evidence: The managed-auth page explains the concept of Composio-managed OAuth apps but does not list toolkits or a Twitter/slug 'twitter' entry; the directory is loaded dynamically ('Loading toolkits...'), and the page says to check via the API or toolkit page.

The Composio KB says 'Composio-managed credentials are not available for the Twitter toolkit... since managed Twitter credentials were removed in February 2026,' and requires a customer-owned OAuth app plus a custom auth config.

The KB says search/counts, post lookup by IDs, post usage, label-stream and compliance-job actions 'read the Application Bearer Token from the Twitter auth config,' and that if these return 401, verify the bearer token comes from the same X Developer App and that the app's plan allows the endpoint.

The KB says 'client-not-enrolled' and 'App not linked to project' usually mean the app is not connected to a project or the OAuth configuration is stale; it advises fixing the app and, if the connection is EXPIRED, recreating it.

The X support page lists logging in and verifying email ('phone number verification... may be needed'), entering developer account name, location and use case details, accepting the developer agreement, and checking email for 'Verify your X Developer Account.'

The Composio guide says to go to https://console.x.com/, 'Click Apps in the left panel,' 'Click on Create App,' 'Click User authentication settings,' select the app type for OAuth 2.0, add the Composio callback URL, and 'store the client ID and secret.'

The Developer Policy says X reviews all proposed uses and that the use case description is binding; a substantive change needs notice and approval before using X Content for the new purpose. Use beyond the Free/Basic/Pro scope requires an Enterprise plan, and X may 'suspend or permanently revoke' access.

The Developer Policy supports that X may suspend or permanently revoke access for policy violations and that failure to follow the approved use case may result in enforcement/suspension. However, it does not present a list of official 'rejection and suspension reasons'; the closest rejection language is that access requests 'rejected for compliance reasons' cannot be reopened, without enumerating reasons.
